**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 23</mark>**<sup>**rd**</sup> **<mark>May 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for February 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for February 2011 world copper supply and demand in its May 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for February 2011 showed a small production deficit of 17,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, February showed a smaller deficit of 9,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first 2 months of 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 60,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 72,000 t). This compares with a production surplus of 119,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 118,000 t) in the same period of 2010. 

During the first 2 months of 2011, world apparent usage of copper grew by 5.9% (approximately 170,000t) compared with that in the same period of 2010, principally owing to the continued recovery in usage levels in the European Union (EU), Japan, and the United States, where usage grew by 6.7%, 5.5%, and 6.3% respectively.  The Russian Federation was also an important contributor to growth with an increase in apparent usage of around 85% in the first two months of 2011. Chinese apparent usage* remained practically unchanged in the period as a 12% increase in January was offset by a fall of 11.8% in February due to lower net imports. 

World mine production grew by around 1% (28,000 t) in the first two months of 2011 compared with that in the same period of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 1.9% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) declined by 1.8%. In part, this relative increase reflects operational constraints that reduced production in early 2010 in Australia, Chile and Mexico. Compared with average daily production in the 4<sup>th</sup> quarter 2010, however, average daily production in the first two months of 2011 was down by 8%. This is reflected in the capacity utilization rate that fell to around 76.5% in January/February from 84% in 4<sup>th</sup> quarter 2010. 

During the first two months of 2011, world refined production remained practically unchanged compared with that in the same period of 2010: Primary production declined by 0.3% and secondary production (from scrap) decreased by 0.2%. Growth in Australia (recovery from low 2010 level), China and Africa were offset by declines in Chile, the United Sates, Canada and Japan. Refined production capacity utilization in the first 2 months of 2011 was around 77% as compared to 79% in the same period of 2010. 

The average LME cash price for May 2011 was US$9,483.25 per tonne, down from the April 2011 average of US$9,530.65 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of April were US$10,148 and US$9,330 per tonne,

respectively, and the average was US$9,609.49 per tonne. As of the end of April 2011, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 678,241 t, an increase of 110,059 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010.
